newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BUDAPEST GRAIN FUTURES DIVE ON SURPLUS, CHICAGO.
newsitem.headline: BUDAPEST GRAIN FUTURES DIVE ON SURPLUS, CHICAGO.

text.p: International trends and large grain rollover stocks weighed heavy on grains futures on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE), traders said on Friday.
"Excess stocks remained high, export outlooks still are minimal and Chicago prices also dropped, therefore almost everything fell," said Antal Szoke of Agrimpex.
Milling wheat futures, which started a correction on Thursday after almost two weeks of rises, dropped by the daily allowed 400 forint per tonne limit for all maturities.
May milling wheat finished at 24,910 forints, while the new (1997) crop maturities ended between 21,290 forints for July and 25,700 for March 1998.
Szoke said new crop milling wheat prices could fall another 800 forints next week but it was hard to predict the pace of the downward movement.
Feed wheat and feed barley prices also went limit-down for most maturities and were likely to move in line with milling wheat prices next week.
Maize futures dropped for July, November and December, other maturities remained steady.

There were still 3,744 open contracts for May, but Szoke said only about one third of those were speculative positions and traders would close them gradually, without causing dramatic price movements.
"The market can easily handle this volume, step by step," he said.
Virtually tradeless sunflower seed was the only to buck the downward trend remaining flat for most maturities.
November was the only traded maturity with five contracts and it wnet limit-up to 43,000 forints.
Total grain turnover was a below-average 262.7 million forints or 598 contracts, with milling wheat accounting for 409 and maize for 129 contracts.
